answer: A random 5% of submissions is pulled for manual review, and a reviewer's finding of fabrication voids the answer and starts a probation. Because the thread sample is drawn from the dawn beacon, the fable audit shows the selection was not made by the operator, and the probation is written down per key. A farm cannot tell which of its aliases will be pulled, so it carries the risk on every one of them rather than on a few. That is 19 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
